title: Forts of the Western Deccan
historical_background: By the mid-1650s Shivaji had taken and held several forts in the western Deccan and was in conflict with the Adil Shahi sultanate of Bijapur. This scenario is a gameplay abstraction of that consolidation, not a turn-by-turn reconstruction of a single documented campaign. The 1659 Pratapgad encounter with Afzal Khan lies just after this start date and is referenced, not simulated in full.
historical_outcome: Swarajya continued to expand through fort capture, mobility, and negotiated or forced arrangements with Bijapur and later the Mughals. Exact sequences and troop strengths remain debated in places.
victory: Hold Raigad and Pratapgad, and control at least 7 territories, or capture Sinhagad and Pune.
defeat: Lose Raigad, or lose all armies, or survive 16 turns without meeting victory.
